subject: Processor controls: request for sampling plan & dataflow diagrams
messages:
From: Erin Martin <erin.martin@clearpay.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@clearpay.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Processor controls: request for sampling plan & dataflow diagrams

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the call this morning — ClearPay is getting closer to procurement approval but our security and privacy team have a couple of follow-ups before we can sign the DPA. Specifically: we've been asked to get a sampling plan for evidence collection (how you'll extract samples of processing logs / audit trails) and the latest dataflow diagrams that show where ClearPay data resides and which subprocessors process specific categories (PII, payment tokens, logs).

Would Redwood be able to:
- Share a short sampling plan that outlines the steps, expected artifacts, and estimated timeline (we typically request a 5–7 business day window to validate),
- Provide the most recent dataflow diagram and a mapping of subprocessors to processing activities (and whether any subprocessors are outside the EEA),
- Confirm whether we can run a scoped audit sampling (3–5 records) or whether you prefer to provide extracts and attestations?

Attachments: we included our privacy questionnaire (attached) to highlight which artifacts we need.

Can you confirm next steps and an ETA? We are targeting a procurement decision by the end of September.

Best,
Erin Martin
Data Protection Officer | ClearPay
er in.martin@clearpay.com
+44 20 7123 4567

Hi Erin — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to support this and Ive looped in Laura (privacy program) and Ben (legal) so they can scope the artifacts. High level: we can provide a sampl ing plan, the latest dataflow diagram, and a mapping of subprocessors by processing activity. We also do scoped extraction under NDA where appropriate.

A couple quick clarifying questions so we scope correctly:
- For the sampling plan, do you want production-sourced logs (redacted) or a synthetic sample derived from production schema?
- What categories count for you as PII vs. tokenized payment information so we can mark the extraction fields?
- Do you require subprocessors to be isolated by country (i.e., list of EEA vs non-EEA) or is a table sufficient?

We anticipate the initial packet (diagram + subprocessor table + controls summary) in 3 business days once we agree scope. If ClearPay prefers a live walk-through or recorded session, we can schedule that as well.

I'll coordinate the attachments and next steps — Laura, Ben: can you confirm the extraction checklist and sample size you recommend for external review?

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Head of Privacy & Trust | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Processor controls: request for sampling plan & dataflow diagrams

Folks — proposed approach for evidence delivery and sampling:

1) Packet contents (deliverable within 3 business days):
- redwood-processor-controls-summary.pdf (SOC-like summary of access controls, auth, logging, retention)
- redwood-dataflow-diagram.vsdx (visio showing ClearPay-identifiable flows: ingest -> store -> inference -> logs)
- subprocessor-mapping.csv (subprocessor, activity, country, legal basis)

2) Sampling plan (separate workbook):
- sample-extraction-plan.xlsx will include: extraction script description, fields to be redacted, sample size (we propose 5 random production records), hashing/one-way anonymization steps for sensitive fields, and verification checklist for ClearPay reviewers.
- We recommend providing redacted production samples under a written attestation and a limited-access TLS link (no direct DB queries). If ClearPay needs direct scoped access to logs, we can propose a screen-shared session with masking.

3) Timeline & gating:
- Dock 3 business days to assemble artifacts (Sep 18 EOD target).
- If ClearPay requests a live forensic extraction, add 2–3 business days for scheduling and approvals.

4) Signatures & legal: Ben, please confirm whether we need a separate DPA addendum to allow production-sourced sample extracts and the appropriate attestation language.

I'll start assembling the diagrams and the control summary today.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
Privacy Program Manager | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Hi Erin — following up with the deliverables we discussed. Attached are: redwood-processor-controls-summary.pdf, redwood-dataflow-diagram.vsdx, and sample-extraction-plan.xlsx (final). I've also uploaded these to a restricted Drive folder and included an access link below.

Key notes:
- Sample type: production-derived, redacted, one-way hashed PII fields (we show the redaction/hashing column in the workbook).
- Sample size: 5 records (randomly selected window); if you need 10 we can expand but it will add one business day.
- Subprocessor mapping: column B in the spreadsheet shows activity-level mapping and country. Two subprocessors are located outside the EEA; both are covered by SCCs and internal transfer assessments.
- Audit access: we can provide a timeboxed screen-share of the log extraction if you require live validation. Alternatively, the extracts + attestation should satisfy procurement in most cases.

Next steps if acceptable:
1) Erin / ClearPay confirm whether extracts are sufficient or if you require a live session.
2) If extracts: provide list of reviewers and we will provision a short-lived link (7-day TTL).
3) If live session: propose Sep 22–23 for a 60-minute walkthrough.

Links and attachments:
